verbalization: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin is implicated in targeting the High affinity immunoglobulin gamma Fc receptor I through a series of molecular interactions. The evidence suggests that gemtuzumab ozogamicin acts as a target for two distinct low-affinity immunoglobulin gamma Fc receptor isoforms, III-A and III-B, which in turn are targeted by cetuximab and midostaurin, respectively. These compounds are known to inhibit the high-affinity Fc receptor I, which is a critical receptor for IgG antibodies in immune-mediated processes. The presence of a final score of 0.5821 in path_421953 and 0.5746 in path_421954 indicates a plausible, though not definitive, relationship between gemtuzumab ozogamicin and the high-affinity Fc receptor I. The mechanism likely involves the binding of gemtuzumab ozogamicin to the low-affinity Fc receptors, which then modulate the activity of the high-affinity receptor I, potentially through a feedback loop or by altering the cellular environment. This suggests that the observed targeting of the high-affinity receptor I may be a downstream effect of the interaction between gemtuzumab ozogamicin and the low-affinity Fc receptors, highlighting a complex, multi-step pathway that warrants further investigation.
